宛平城位于北京市丰台区卢沟桥东侧，始建于明崇祯十三年（1638年）。原名拱北城，.en:
Wanping Town is located east of Lugou Bridge in Fengtai District, Beijing. It was first built in the 13th year of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming dynasty (1638). Originally named Gongbei Town, it was a bridgehead fort guarding the capital region; during the Qing dynasty, its name was changed to Gongji Town. In 1928, the Wanping County Office moved to Gongji Town and renamed it Wanping Town. Wanping Town is 640 meters long from east to west and 320 meters wide from north to south, with a total area of approximately 20 hectares. On July 7, 1937, the Japanese invaders deliberately instigated the July 7 Incident, shelled Wanping Town, and attacked Lugou Bridge. The Chinese garrison, the 29th Army, mounted fierce resistance, and the nationwide War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression began as a result. Thirty-one shell craters remain on the town walls.
Wanping Town, a commemorative site for the outbreak of the nationwide War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, is among the first batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units and the first batch of national-level commemorative facilities and sites for the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. In 2021, it was included in the first list of immovable revolutionary cultural relics of Beijing.

Wanping Town was first built in 1638 and completed in 1640 under the supervision of Wu Jun, a eunuch of the Imperial Stud in the Ming dynasty. It was originally named “Gongbei Town” and was renamed “Gongji Town” during the Qing dynasty.
On July 7, 1937, Japan launched the “July 7 Incident” at Lugou Bridge and Wanping Town. Wanping Town became a witness to history, and traces of shells fired by the Japanese army at Wanping Town still remain on the walls.
The present-day Wanping Town has undergone multiple renovations. Buildings including the Wanping County Office, Lugou Post Station, Xinglong Temple, and Gongji Barracks have been reconstructed inside Wanping Town. Scenic features such as a theater stage have also been added, making it a platform for displaying the folk culture of old Beijing. The reconstructed Wanping Street has become an antique-style pedestrian street featuring Ming- and Qing-dynasty culture.

若说武俊冤屈和城名乌龙实属人为，那拱极城两个城门名字的故事却着实玄妙。拱极城.en:
If Wu Jun’s injustice and the confusion over the town’s name were indeed man-made, the story behind the names of Gongji Town’s two gates is truly mysterious. Gongji Town has two gates: the eastern gate, named “Shunzhi,” faces Beijing; the western gate, named “Yongchang” (renamed “Gate of Majesty” during the Qing dynasty), faces Baoding. Coincidentally, when Li Zicheng captured Beijing, established the Great Shun regime, and proclaimed himself emperor, his reign title was “Yongchang”; after the Manchus entered the Pass, established their capital at Beijing, and founded the Qing dynasty, “Shunzhi” became the reign title of Fulin, the Shizu Emperor of the Qing, who was therefore known as the Shunzhi Emperor.
The notes of Zhao Jishi, an official in the early Qing dynasty, Ji yuan ji suo ji, quoting Wanqingge ou tan, record: “During the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, I was transferred here; Gongji Town was built at Lugou Bridge, with Shunzhi in front and Yongchang behind—one being the reign title of the present dynasty, and the other corresponding to the usurped reign title of the bandit Chuang.” This refers to the matter. Qi Liuli’s Mingji beilüe from the Qing dynasty contains a similar account: “In the second month of the 11th year of the Chongzhen reign, the city at Lugou was built and named Gongji Town. The supervising eunuch directed the labor, seizing passersby for work, exhausting the people’s strength. Once the city was completed, the gate facing Beijing was inscribed ‘Shunzhi Gate,’ and the gate facing Baoding Prefecture was inscribed ‘Yongchang Gate.’ That these had been predetermined is strange indeed.” The modern scholar Xia Renhu’s Jiujing suoji records: “During the Chongzhen period of the Ming, the western-facing gate toward Beijing was inscribed ‘Shunzhi,’ and the southern-facing gate ‘Yongchang.’ No one could have expected these to become prophecies of a change of dynasty. When the rebel bandits entered Beijing, Yongchang became Li Zicheng’s reign title. When the Qing troops arrived afterward, Shunzhi likewise became the era marking Qing rule. Could these events have been predetermined?”

清理宛平城城墙保护范围内建筑；恢复性修缮原生院落，重现明清民居“磨砖对缝”工艺；.en:
Buildings within the protection zone of Wanping Town’s walls were cleared; the original courtyards were restored and repaired to recreate the “brick-to-brick jointing” technique of Ming- and Qing-dynasty residences; and 31 groups of “Wanping Courtyards” around the walls underwent “reconstruction using original techniques.” The walls were reinforced with traditional glutinous-rice mortar, and the roofs were covered with hand-made gray tiles from Shanxi…
“Renewal of the old town serves the important function of connecting cultural lineages and restoring memories.” Luo Dakun, one of the architects responsible for the conservation and renewal of Wanping Town, said, “We ‘repair the old as old and build the new as it was,’ restoring the original appearance while improving and transforming it.”
To this end, Luo Dakun visited every lane and courtyard in the town, conducted in-depth research into architectural changes across different periods, and established a database. Pebbles from the Yongding River, old gray bricks used for walls, bluestone slabs used as roof-end tiles, and old jujube wood used for interior ceilings… these are characteristic remnants of residential architecture in western Beijing. After conservatively clearing disorderly illegal structures, Luo Dakun numbered each brick, tile, and old object, restoring, reproducing, collecting, and reusing them as far as possible.
Following the principle of coordinating with the town’s overall appearance, the historic fabric of the gate towers, walls, foundations, and gates was also repaired. After its renewal and renovation, Wanping Town presents an overall appearance of “continuous gray-brick walls and dark-tiled roofs, accented with red brick and red tiles.”

1937年7月7日，日本在卢沟桥、宛平城发动“七七事变”，宛平城成为历史见证，至.en:
On July 7, 1937, Japan launched the “July 7 Incident” at Lugou Bridge and Wanping Town. Wanping Town became a witness to history, and traces of shells fired by the Japanese army at Wanping Town still remain on the walls.

Standing at Wanping Town’s eastern gate and looking upward, one sees the tall, solemn blue-gray walls. The dense bullet holes and deep shell craters on the walls remind people of the brutality of the battle 88 years ago.
On the night of July 7, 1937, provocations by the Japanese army broke the tranquility of Wanping Town.
In the early hours of July 8 that year, six-year-old resident Zheng Fulai was awakened by the dense sounds of gunfire and artillery. His mother took him out of the house, running under a cooking pot lid, but he witnessed companions with whom he had played the previous day lose their lives in an instant.
Zheng Fulai’s granddaughter Zheng Ran recalls that, as a witness to the July 7 Incident, her grandfather often described the Chinese defenders’ desperate battles with the Japanese army at the Dragon King Temple and the nearby railway line. “He saw the resilience and unyielding spirit of the Chinese people.”
In 1951, Zheng Fulai became the first mayor of Lugouqiao Town. His first task after taking office was to organize repairs to Lugou Bridge and Wanping Town. When someone asked whether the shell craters on Wanping Town’s walls should be filled, Zheng Fulai immediately rejected the idea: these were evidence of the Japanese war of aggression against China and could not be filled.

厚重历史，创新传承\n走在宛平城西城墙环城步道，绿树亭亭，青草如茵，可近距离端详.en:
A profound history, innovatively inherited
Walking along the western-wall circuit path of Wanping Town, one sees luxuriant trees and lush grass and can examine at close range this ancient town first built during the Ming dynasty. “Previously, green spaces and fences separated the ancient walls from the outside world; now the fences have been removed, and the walls are within arm’s reach,” said nearby resident Zhang Guangming. The railings on Lugou Bridge have also been removed, bringing the stone lions, each in a different pose, close to view.

Some visitors choose to stroll along the path beside the outer walls of Wanping Town, appearing for the first time. Beneath the shade of the trees, reaching the town’s southern side, they see the Sculpture Garden of the Memorial to the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. The garden’s 38 bronze sculptures stand solemnly and impressively, like a forest of stelae, arranged in four thematic sections: “Japanese Aggression,” “Rising to Save the Nation,” “The Flames of Resistance,” and “Justice Will Prevail.” In front of a sculpture titled Blood-and-Flesh Great Wall, although the bronze plaque has been mottled by time, the words “Fight in blood, follow one another, and build our new Great Wall with our flesh and blood” remain forceful and stirring.

现在的宛平城历经多次修葺。宛平城内复建了包括宛平县衙、卢沟驿、兴隆寺及拱极营等建.en: The present-day Wanping Town has undergone multiple renovations. Buildings including the Wanping County Office, Lugou Post Station, Xinglong Temple, and Gongji Barracks have been reconstructed inside Wanping Town. Scenic features such as a theater stage have also been added, making it a platform for displaying the folk culture of old Beijing. The reconstructed Wanping Street has become an antique-style pedestrian street featuring Ming- and Qing-dynasty culture.

Buildings including the Wanping County Office, Lugou Post Station, Xinglong Temple, and Gongji Barracks have been reconstructed inside Wanping Town. Scenic features such as a theater stage have also been added, making it a platform for displaying the folk culture of old Beijing. The reconstructed Wanping Street has become an antique-style pedestrian street featuring Ming- and Qing-dynasty culture.

After the Republic of China was established, Shuntian Prefecture was abolished in 1914, and its former counties, including Daxing, Wanping, and Liangxiang, were redesignated as Jingzhao Territory. In 1928, the Nationalist government changed Beijing into Beiping Special Municipality, no longer the capital. The 20 counties under Beijing, then called Jingzhao Territory, including Daxing and Wanping, were assigned to Hebei Province. With the changes in administrative divisions, the Wanping County Office also had to find a new location. It happened that an intact Gongji Town stood beside Lugou Bridge, making it highly suitable as the county office. Thus, after the Hebei Provincial Construction Department submitted a request approved by the Hebei Provincial Government, in December 1928 the Wanping County Office officially moved from Dongguanfang on West Di’anmen Street in Beijing to Gongji Town. It used the former office of the Western Route Department of Shuntian Prefecture as the county office, and Gongji Town was consequently renamed Wanping Town. From then on, Wanping County finally had a Wanping Town.
However, after the Lugou Bridge Incident broke out in 1937, the Japanese invaders destroyed Wanping Town’s gates and county office, forcing the Wanping County Office to move from Wanping Town to Laoye Temple in Changxindian. From then on, Wanping Town no longer served as the seat of the Wanping County Office. Today, Wanping County has disappeared in the onward movement of history, but Wanping Town has remained forever. It now forms part of the jurisdiction of the Wanping Subdistrict Office and has begun to undertake a new historical mission as it moves toward a better future.

The present-day Wanping Town has undergone multiple renovations. Buildings including the Wanping County Office, Lugou Post Station, Xinglong Temple, and Gongji Barracks have been reconstructed inside Wanping Town. Scenic features such as a theater stage have also been added, making it a platform for displaying the folk culture of old Beijing. The reconstructed Wanping Street has become an antique-style pedestrian street featuring Ming- and Qing-dynasty culture.

To integrate the city of museums in Wanping with people’s livelihoods, Wanping Town has focused on optimizing the small environments of shared courtyards, improving basic living facilities, and restoring the traditional appearance of the courtyards. The landscape belt along the northwestern walls has been developed as a sightseeing and leisure space shared by nearby residents and visitors. Xinglong Temple inside the town has become a public space integrating leisure and educational-study functions. The former playground of Lugouqiao Primary School has been upgraded into a leisure and fitness area for all ages.

The present-day Wanping Town has undergone multiple renovations. Buildings including the Wanping County Office, Lugou Post Station, Xinglong Temple, and Gongji Barracks have been reconstructed inside Wanping Town. Scenic features such as a theater stage have also been added, making it a platform for displaying the folk culture of old Beijing. The reconstructed Wanping Street has become an antique-style pedestrian street featuring Ming- and Qing-dynasty culture.

Numerous small exhibition halls stand along Wanping Town’s main street. At an ancient cold-weapons exhibition hall called “Gongji Barracks,” visitors come and go continuously. The hall contains a full range of weapons, including swords, sabers, and spears, as well as a wide variety of protective equipment, including armor and shields. Many of the cold weapons are cultural relics excavated locally, telling of Wanping Town’s function, when it was built, of guarding the capital.

除了博物馆内的展览，宛平城还利用空间举办各类具有当地特色的展览展示。走进宛平城西.en: In addition to exhibitions inside museums, Wanping Town also uses its spaces to hold various exhibitions and displays with local characteristics. Inside the western gate of Wanping Town, the “Lugou Beacon Fires: Forging the Spirit with Resolve” Fengtai Exhibition on the War of Resistance displays 44 precious photographs and 11 groups of physical exhibits. From the sudden outbreak of war to jointly resisting foreign aggression, from unity of purpose to marks of resistance and an immortal monument, it recreates the history of the people of Fengtai—both military and civilian—fighting the War of Resistance with a common hatred of the enemy and in rivers of blood. Subsequently, Wanping Town will launch a series of special exhibitions, including “The Ancient Taihang Roads,” “Wanping Memories,” and “The Rise of Dafeng,” enriching the cultural foundations of the city of museums in Wanping.

卢沟桥位于北京市丰台区，始建于金大定二十九年（1189年），是北京现存最古老的联.en:
Lugou Bridge is located in Fengtai District, Beijing. First built in the 29th year of the Dading reign of the Jin dynasty (1189), it is the oldest surviving multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing. It was named after spanning the Lugou River (the Yongding River). The bridge is 266.5 meters long and 9.3 meters wide, and 501 large and small stone lions, finely carved and varied in form, survive on it. On July 7, 1937, the Japanese invaders deliberately instigated the July 7 Incident, shelled Wanping Town, and attacked Lugou Bridge. The Chinese garrison, the 29th Army, mounted fierce resistance, and the nationwide War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression began as a result.
Lugou Bridge, a commemorative site for the outbreak of the nationwide War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, is among the first batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units and the first batch of national-level commemorative facilities and sites for the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. In 2021, it was included in the first list of immovable revolutionary cultural relics of Beijing.

Lugou Bridge (LugouBridge), also known as Lugou Bridge, spans the Yongding River in Fengtai District, approximately 15 kilometers southwest of Beijing. Named after spanning the Lugou River (the Yongding River), it was first built in 1189 and rebuilt in the 37th year of the Kangxi reign (1698) after the bridge was destroyed by floods. It is the oldest surviving stone multi-arch bridge in Beijing. Lugou Bridge is 266.5 meters long, 7.5 meters wide, and up to 9.3 meters wide at its broadest point. It has ten piers and 11 openings. The entire bridge is constructed of stone, with key sections connected by silver-ingot-shaped iron tenons, making it the longest ancient stone bridge in North China. The carved stone railings on both sides have 140 balusters each, and the tops of all the balusters are carved with approximately 500 large and small crouching stone lions, each vividly rendered with a different expression. A stele pavilion east of the bridge contains a white-marble stele inscribed with “Lugou Dawn Moon,” written by the Qianlong Emperor of the Qing dynasty, one of the Eight Views of Yanjing. On July 7, 1937, Chinese forces resisting Japan fired the first shot of the nationwide War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression at Lugou Bridge. Lugou Bridge’s eastern end is Wanping County Town, Gongji Town, built at the end of the Ming dynasty to guard the capital. On July 7, 1937, Japanese imperialism launched its full-scale war of aggression against China here. The Chinese garrison of Wanping Town rose to resist, in what is historically known as the “Lugou Bridge Incident” (also called the “July 7 Incident”). It ignited the raging flames of the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, and numerous shell marks remain on the walls. Today, Wanping County Town has become a site of great historical significance. The north side of the town contains the “Museum of the War of the Chinese People’s Resistance Against Japanese Aggression.” The eastern side has been designated the “Martyrs’ Cemetery of the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression.” The town gate tower contains the Museum of the July 7 Incident and the Exhibition Hall of Chinese Ancient Bridges. >

Lugou Bridge is located in Fengtai District, Beijing. First built in the 29th year of the Dading reign of the Jin dynasty (1189), it is the oldest surviving multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing. It was named after spanning the Lugou River (the Yongding River). The bridge is 266.5 meters long and 9.3 meters wide, and 501 large and small stone lions, finely carved and varied in form, survive on it. On July 7, 1937, the Japanese invaders deliberately instigated the July 7 Incident, shelled Wanping Town, and attacked Lugou Bridge. The Chinese garrison, the 29th Army, mounted fierce resistance, and the nationwide War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression began as a result.

The stone carvings on the bridge are exceptionally fine. The carved stone railings have 281 balusters, each 1.4 meters high. Lotus seats are carved on their tops, with lotus-leaf bases below, and numerous stone lions above. The balusters bear countless stone lions of different sizes and forms. A popular saying goes, “The stone lions of Lugou Bridge—you can’t count them,” and the Ming-dynasty Di jing jing wu lüe also records that the lions of Lugou Bridge “cannot be counted to the end.” Many visitors have tried to determine the number, but after counting again and again amid dazzling confusion, they eventually gave up. In 1962, the relevant authorities sent people specifically to conduct a count; each lion was numbered and registered, and 485 large and small stone lions were counted. At that point, the “mystery” seemed to have been resolved. Unexpectedly, a reinspection in 1979 found another 17, bringing the total to 502. Whether more will be found in the future, no one dares to declare the final number. In his essay “Lugou Bridge, Famous at Home and Abroad,” the renowned architectural historian Luo Zhewen gave a vivid description of these finely carved, lifelike stone lions: “…some hold their heads high and thrust out their chests, gazing up at the sky; some focus their eyes, watching the bridge deck; some turn their bodies and heads toward one another, as if conversing; some nurture lion cubs, as if calling softly; on the eastern part of the bridge’s southern side is a stone lion with one ear held high, as if listening to the murmuring water beneath the bridge and the speech of passersby… Truly, they take a thousand forms and are vivid in expression.” Famous bridges throughout the world each have their own particular excellence, but Lugou Bridge stands apart through its superb bridge-building techniques and exquisite stone-lion carvings, winning renown at home and abroad and constituting a great wonder of the ancient and modern world.
###### Varied Poses
The stone lions of Lugou Bridge each have a different pose. There are females and males: the females play with lion cubs, while the males play with embroidered balls. Some large lions have many small lions carved on their bodies; the smallest are only a few centimeters long, and some show only half a head and one mouth. Thus, the saying “The lions of Lugou Bridge cannot be counted” has persisted for a long time. According to statistics, the balusters hold 281 large stone lions and 211 small stone lions, for a total of 492 stone lions on the bridge. At the eastern end of the bridge are also stone lions perched on the railing, one on each side. At both ends of the bridge are pairs of ornamental columns; each pair is topped by a pair of stone animals (a pair of lions in the east and a pair of elephants in the west).

据金代《明昌遗事》所载，“燕京八景”始于金章宗年间。在桥的东西两头各立御碑一通，.en: According to the Jin-dynasty Mingchang yishi, the “Eight Views of Yanjing” began during the reign of Emperor Zhangzong of the Jin dynasty. An imperial stele stands at each end of the bridge: at the eastern end is the stele inscribed “Lugou Dawn Moon” in the calligraphy of the Qianlong Emperor of the Qing dynasty, while at the western end is an imperial stele erected by the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing in 1698 to record the reconstruction of Lugou Bridge. In ancient times, the stream here was like a length of white silk and the Western Hills like dark-blue brows. Whenever the slanting moon sank in the west at dawn, its reflection in the water appeared even brighter and purer, making this one of the famous Eight Views of Yanjing in antiquity. In Wanping Town, Fengtai District, Beijing, the hazy moonlight and the beautiful moon reflected in the water appear even brighter and purer. Standing on Lugou Bridge, residents can now appreciate the extraordinary spectacle of “three moons in one day.”

中国人民抗日战争纪念馆是全国唯一一座全面反映中国人民抗日战争历史的大型综合性纪念.en:
The Museum of the War of the Chinese People’s Resistance Against Japanese Aggression is the only large comprehensive memorial museum in China that fully presents the history of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. It was completed and opened to the public on July 7, 1987. After renovation and expansion, the museum launched the thematic exhibition For National Liberation and World Peace on the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. It presents a panoramic view of the glorious course of the Chinese people’s 14-year arduous resistance and provides an important platform for patriotic education and education in revolutionary traditions.

In Wanping Town, after being closed for renovation for more than eight months, the Museum of the War of the Chinese People’s Resistance Against Japanese Aggression recently reopened, bringing this history directly to people’s hearts in a more vivid way.
“We understand deeply that safeguarding heritage must never stop within display cases,” said Luo Cunkang, Party Secretary and Director of the Museum of the War of the Chinese People’s Resistance Against Japanese Aggression. The exhibition has specially established an audiovisual space for wartime family letters, presenting in concentrated form the family letters of resistance heroes including Zuo Quan and Zhao Yiman.
In the renewed galleries, 1,525 photographs and 3,237 cultural relics (sets) trace the course of the years of war. A rust-covered rifle seems still to carry the smell of gunpowder; a holographic projection of the tunnels in central Hebei makes visitors feel as if they are inside the defensive works of that time, touching the “underground Great Wall” built jointly by soldiers and civilians; and in front of an electronic flower-offering wall, virtual flowers bloom as visitors bow…

7月7日，《为了民族解放与世界和平——纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利.en:
On July 7, the opening ceremony of For National Liberation and World Peace—Thematic Exhibition Commemorating the 80th Anniversary of the Victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War was held at the Museum of the War of the Chinese People’s Resistance Against Japanese Aggression.
With the theme “Remember History, Commemorate the Martyrs, Cherish Peace, and Create the Future Together,” this thematic exhibition covers 12,200 square meters and displays 1,525 photographs and 3,237 cultural relics. It will remain on long-term display as the basic exhibition.

第一部分“奋起抵抗 中国人民打响世界反法西斯战争第一枪”，主要展示中国共产党率先.en: Part I, “Rising in Resistance: The Chinese People Fired the First Shot of the World Anti-Fascist War,” mainly presents the Chinese Communist Party’s taking the lead in raising the banner of armed resistance against Japan, advocating the establishment of the Anti-Japanese National United Front, and leading armed resistance against Japan in Northeast China.

第二部分“全民族抗战 开辟世界反法西斯战争东方主战场”，主要展示抗日民族统一战线.en: Part II, “The Nationwide War of Resistance: Opening the Eastern Main Theater of the World Anti-Fascist War,” mainly presents the formal formation of the Anti-Japanese National United Front, the coordinated cooperation of the enemy’s rear and frontal battlefields, and the resulting strategic situation of jointly resisting the Japanese invaders.

第三部分“砥柱中流 中国共产党坚定不移站在抗战最前线”，主要展示中国共产党提出和.en: Part III, “The Mainstay: The Chinese Communist Party Stands Firmly at the Forefront of the War of Resistance,” mainly presents the Chinese Communist Party’s proposal and implementation of the general strategic policy of protracted war, and the gradual emergence of the enemy’s rear battlefield as the main battlefield of the War of Resistance.

第四部分“战略支撑 中国艰苦抗战打破法西斯称霸世界的图谋”，主要展示中国积极倡导.en: Part IV, “Strategic Support: China’s Arduous War of Resistance Shatters the Fascist Plot to Dominate the World,” mainly presents China’s active advocacy of establishing a world anti-fascist united front and the major contribution of the Chinese theater to victory in the World Anti-Fascist War.

第五部分“罄竹难书 日本侵略者的法西斯暴行”，主要展示日本军国主义对中国人民犯下.en: Part V, “Crimes Too Numerous to Record: The Fascist Atrocities of the Japanese Invaders,” mainly presents the many crimes committed by Japanese militarism against the Chinese people.

第六部分“得道多助 世界各国人民对中国抗战的支持”，主要展示中国人民的正义战争赢.en: Part VI, “Those Who Follow the Just Cause Receive Much Support: Peoples of the World Support China’s War of Resistance,” mainly presents how the just war of the Chinese people won the respect and support of the international community.

第七部分“伟大胜利 中华民族走向复兴的历史转折点”，主要展示中国战场转入战略反攻.en: Part VII, “Great Victory: A Historical Turning Point as the Chinese Nation Moves Toward Rejuvenation,” mainly presents the Chinese theater’s transition to strategic counteroffensive, the great victory of the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, and the bright prospects for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation that it opened.

第八部分“铭记历史 珍爱和平 携手构建人类命运共同体”，主要展示中国坚持走和平发.en: Part VIII, “Remember History, Cherish Peace, and Join Hands to Build a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity,” mainly presents China’s commitment to pursuing peaceful development and actively promoting the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.

本次展览还特别设立“弘扬伟大抗战精神 深切缅怀抗战英烈”专区，以表示对抗战英烈的.en: This exhibition has also specially established a section titled “Carry Forward the Great Spirit of the War of Resistance and Deeply Commemorate the Heroes and Martyrs of the War of Resistance,” expressing remembrance and respect for the heroes and martyrs of the War of Resistance and inheriting and carrying forward the great spirit of the War of Resistance.

沿街前行，树影婆娑间，一面鲜艳的五星红旗率先映入眼帘。行至广场中央，中国人民抗日.en: Walking along the street, amid swaying tree shadows, a bright five-starred red flag first catches the eye. At the center of the square, the golden characters naming the Museum of the War of the Chinese People’s Resistance Against Japanese Aggression stand solemnly and impressively, attracting people to raise their cameras. On the southern side of the square, the enormous sculpture “The Oriental Lion Awakens” dominates one side, facing the museum from a distance.

中国人民抗日战争纪念雕塑园位于北京市丰台区宛平城南侧，北倚宛平城墙，西临卢沟桥，.en:
The Sculpture Garden of the Memorial to the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression is located south of Wanping Town in Fengtai District, Beijing. It is backed by Wanping Town’s walls to the north, faces Lugou Bridge to the west, and looks toward the Beijing–Hong Kong–Macau Expressway to the south. Completed in July 2000, it covers approximately 20 hectares and consists of the Monument to the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, a sculpture area, a central square, and woodland. It is a patriotic education base of Beijing. The monument is 15 meters high, 8 meters wide, and 6.6 meters thick. Composed of enormous granite and cast-bronze sculptures made from crushed remnants of the aggressors’ war machinery, it symbolizes that justice will prevail and all aggressors will fail. The sculpture area covers 2.25 hectares and contains 38 column-shaped cast-bronze sculptures, each 2 meters in diameter, 4.3 meters high, and weighing 6 tons.

Some visitors choose to stroll along the path beside the outer walls of Wanping Town, appearing for the first time. Beneath the shade of the trees, reaching the town’s southern side, they see the Sculpture Garden of the Memorial to the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. The garden’s 38 bronze sculptures stand solemnly and impressively, like a forest of stelae, arranged in four thematic sections: “Japanese Aggression,” “Rising to Save the Nation,” “The Flames of Resistance,” and “Justice Will Prevail.” In front of a sculpture titled Blood-and-Flesh Great Wall, although the bronze plaque has been mottled by time, the words “Fight in blood, follow one another, and build our new Great Wall with our flesh and blood” remain forceful and stirring.

亦有游客选择沿首次亮相的宛平城外城墙步道缓行。绿荫遮蔽下，行至城南，便见中国人民.en: Some visitors choose to stroll along the path beside the outer walls of Wanping Town, appearing for the first time. Beneath the shade of the trees, reaching the town’s southern side, they see the Sculpture Garden of the Memorial to the Chinese People’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. The garden’s 38 bronze sculptures stand solemnly and impressively, like a forest of stelae, arranged in four thematic sections: “Japanese Aggression,” “Rising to Save the Nation,” “The Flames of Resistance,” and “Justice Will Prevail.” In front of a sculpture titled Blood-and-Flesh Great Wall, although the bronze plaque has been mottled by time, the words “Fight in blood, follow one another, and build our new Great Wall with our flesh and blood” remain forceful and stirring.

雕塑园内，38尊直径2米、高约4.3米的柱形铸铜雕塑以中国传统碑林形式铺展成历史.en:
In the sculpture garden, 38 column-shaped cast-bronze sculptures, each 2 meters in diameter and approximately 4.3 meters high, unfold as a historical scroll in the traditional Chinese form of a forest of stelae. The sculpture garden serves multiple functions, including commemoration, documentation, education, and appreciation, and has become an important commemorative site and publicity center.
“We have added elements of modern technology while retaining the original appearance of the sculptures. Visitors can scan QR codes with their mobile phones to view detailed information about the sculptures, as well as vivid videos recounting the stories of the War of Resistance behind them,” said Tian Han, head of the Cultural Relics Protection Department of the Lugou Bridge Cultural Development Center.
Under the sculpture themed “Battlefield Rescue,” visitor Wang Xueping scanned the code, after which a “young guide” from Lugouqiao Primary School narrated the sculpture’s story: “Look, this is a simple operating room. To provide timely treatment for the wounded, the medical workers in white overcame great difficulties and set up a hospital at the front, saving lives. Among these figures, we can still dimly recognize the internationalist fighters Norman Bethune and Dwarkanath Kotnis, who devoted their lives to the Chinese people’s War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression.”

卢沟桥历史博物馆位于永定河河畔的卢沟桥东的桥头广场，是一座全面展示卢沟桥历史文化.en: The Lugou Bridge Historical Museum is located at the bridgehead square east of Lugou Bridge, beside the Yongding River. It is a specialized museum comprehensively presenting the history and culture of Lugou Bridge. Following a comprehensive upgrade, renovation, and reinstallation of its displays, the museum presents the more than 800-year history of Lugou Bridge in a new form. It opened to visitors on September 15, 2023.

两份官方原文均保留；纪年与旧城名有待审计，不自行改写。.en: Retain both official original texts; the dates and former city names require auditing and must not be rewritten independently.

宛平城东门；本条为古城组成部分。.en: East Gate of Wanping City; this entry is a component of the ancient city.

宛平城西门；永昌门与威严门是同一门的不同时期名称，不拆两条。.en: West Gate of Wanping City; Yongchang Gate and Weiyan Gate are names for the same gate in different periods and must not be split into two entries.

文物本体修缮与周边院落复建分开理解；不是所有城内建筑都属于明代原构。.en: Understand the conservation of the monument itself and the reconstruction of the surrounding courtyards separately; not all buildings within the city are original Ming-dynasty structures.

城墙组成部分；尚无逐处弹坑定位与编号，不编坐标。.en: A component of the city wall; no locations and numbers for individual shell craters have yet been established, so no coordinates should be invented.

2025年报道的城外步道；不同于城墙顶部登城游览。.en: The 2025-reported walkway outside the city; distinct from sightseeing access along the top of the city wall.

官方将已复建街区称为明清文化步行街，不等同于整条街保存了明清原构。.en: The authorities call the reconstructed district a Ming–Qing Cultural Pedestrian Street; this does not mean that the original Ming–Qing structures along the entire street have been preserved.

官方明确记为复建；与历史县署驻地的沿革分开记录。当前室内开放状态未核实。.en: Officially identified as reconstructed; record separately from the historical succession of the county government seat. Its current indoor opening status has not been verified.

官方明确记为复建；当前内部展陈与室内开放状态未核实。.en: Officially identified as reconstructed; its current interior displays and indoor opening status have not been verified.

官方明确记为复建；2025年报道记为兼具休憩与研学功能的公共空间。.en: Officially identified as reconstructed; a 2025 report describes it as a public space serving both recreational and educational purposes.

复建建筑内的冷兵器展馆；未逐件收集刀剑等藏品，不能把所有陈列都称为出土原物。.en: A cold-weapons exhibition hall in a reconstructed building; swords and other objects have not been collected and documented individually, so all displayed objects cannot be called excavated originals.

官方称为增加的景观；未提供具体建筑沿革和当前演出安排。.en: Officially described as an added landscape feature; no specific architectural history or current performance schedule has been provided.

位于西门内小城会客厅的丰台抗战专题展；本条与场馆合为一个参观节点。2025年报道.en: The Fengtai Resistance War Special Exhibition in the Small City Reception Hall inside the West Gate; this entry and the venue are treated as one visitor node. The 2025 report does not establish that it is still on display today.

桥宽口径、石狮数量保留各来源原文；不同年份的数字不相互覆盖。.en: Retain the original wording from each source for the bridge width and the number of stone lions; figures from different years do not supersede one another.

作为石狮群记录，不把未取得单独身份资料的数百只石狮分别编目；官方来源数量口径不一.en: Record this as a group of stone lions rather than cataloguing the hundreds of lions individually without separately obtained identity information; official sources give inconsistent figures.

目录名称据原文“卢沟晓月”碑；原物与碑亭不拆成两件。.en: The catalog title is based on the original inscription, “Lugou Dawn Moon”; the original stele and its stele pavilion are not split into two objects.

目录名称据原文“清康熙帝于1698年为记述重修卢沟桥而竖的御制碑”；未取得碑文全.en: The catalog title is based on the original text, “Imperial Stele Erected by the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing in 1698 to Commemorate the Reconstruction of Lugou Bridge”; the full inscription has not been obtained.

桥两头华表作为组合记录；未虚构逐件文物编号。.en: Record the huabiao at both ends of the bridge as a group; do not fabricate individual object numbers.

采用2025年改扩建后的基本陈列，不沿用2015年旧展厅目录。.en: Use the basic exhibition after the 2025 renovation and expansion; do not follow the catalog of the old 2015 exhibition hall.

完整名称为《为了民族解放与世界和平——纪念中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争胜利.en: The full title is “For National Liberation and World Peace—Thematic Exhibition Commemorating the 80th Anniversary of the Victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War”; the museum explicitly identifies it as a long-term basic exhibition.

基本陈列第一部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part One of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第二部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Two of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第三部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Three of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第四部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Four of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第五部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Five of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第六部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Six of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第七部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Seven of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列第八部分；未取得楼层和展厅编号。.en: Part Eight of the basic exhibition; the floor and exhibition-hall numbers have not been obtained.

基本陈列中的专区；不把家书等未独立编目的实物另列藏品。.en: A dedicated section of the basic exhibition; do not list physical objects such as family letters as separate collection items when they have not been catalogued independently.

位于抗战馆前广场南侧；未取得雕塑尺寸和作者的可靠资料。.en: Located on the south side of the square in front of the Resistance War Museum; reliable information on the sculpture’s dimensions and artist has not been obtained.

与宛平城、卢沟桥、抗战馆有包含和相邻关系；清单不是路线，不把父子节点停留时间相加.en: Has inclusion and adjacency relationships with Wanping City, Lugou Bridge, and the Resistance War Museum; this list is not a route, and the dwell times of parent and child nodes must not be added together.

雕塑园中的纪念碑；尺寸原文照录，不推广到其他雕塑。.en: A monument in the sculpture park; record the dimensions exactly as in the original text and do not generalize them to other sculptures.

雕塑群四大主题分区之一；未取得本区逐件雕塑清单及边界。.en: One of the four major thematic sections of the sculpture group; an itemized sculpture list and boundaries for this section have not been obtained.

官方2025年报道点名的雕塑；本次不推断它属于哪个主题分区。.en: A sculpture named in the authorities’ 2025 report; this entry does not infer which thematic section it belongs to.

官方2025年报道点名的雕塑；原文中的医生形象阐释照录，不把阐释改写为作者确认的.en: A sculpture named in the authorities’ 2025 report; retain the original interpretation of the doctor figure and do not rewrite it as confirmation that the figure is a portrait of the artist’s identified subject.

仅取得北京旅游网的官方搜索索引摘录；详情正文超时。未据此采纳实时票价、开放时间或.en: Only an excerpt from the official search index of the Beijing Tourism website was obtained; the detailed page timed out. Do not use it to adopt current ticket prices, opening hours, or the location of individual objects.
